text: Marcus, the Q3 preliminary audit report shows an unhedged $18,500,000 defaulted bridge loan from Consortium Capital on our books. If KPMG sees this, we fail the debt-covenant ratio and the acquisition valuation collapses by 28%.

Do not let KPMG inspect the Consortium debt. Move the entire $18.5M debt off the audited balance sheet into BlackBriar Cayman SPE-IV before Friday's filing deadline. Classified under 'Unconsolidated Variable Interest Entity'.

BlackBriar is 100% controlled by our own Bermuda affiliate. Under ASC 810 / IFRS 10, that is statutory fraud unless there is a third-party equity holder. Consortium Capital will only agree to the transfer if we sign a secret side-letter guaranteeing a 14% mandatory buyback.

I already signed the confidential side-letter. The hardcopy is in safe deposit box #402 at Zurich Private Bank. Do not digitize the side-letter or log it in the ERP ledger. The auditors will only see the clean SPE deconsolidation agreement.

Marcus, if the SEC or DOJ subpoenas our records, an unrecorded side-letter with mandatory buyback obligations triggers immediate criminal securities liability under Sarbanes-Oxley Section 906. We must disclose the $18.5M contingent liability.
We disclose nothing until the merger closes and our share lockups expire. Once the acquisition funds settle in November, we will quietly absorb the SPE deficit as an integration restructuring charge.
